root_cause.text: The HFS new mount API conversion allocated filesystem-private state in `sb->s_fs_info` before `hfs_fill_super()` owned it, but cleanup still freed that state only in `hfs_mdb_put()`, so failures in the `sget_fc()`/`setup_bdev_super()` path leaked the `struct hfs_sb_info`.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says that after the new mount API conversion, if `setup_bdev_super()` fails after `sget_fc()` allocates a new superblock but before `hfs_fill_super()` takes ownership, `s_fs_info` is leaked; the patch moves freeing of `HFS_SB(sb)` out of `hfs_mdb_put()` by deleting `kfree(HFS_SB(sb)); sb->s_fs_info = NULL;` and adds `hfs_kill_super()` that calls `kill_block_super(sb); kfree(hsb);`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return -EIO directly when reading the HFS MDB block fails so read errors are reported correctly.
intent_record.what: In hfs_mdb_get(), the error path after sb_bread512() fails was changed from jumping to the out label with 'goto out' to immediately returning '-EIO'.
intent_record.how: When the metadata block read fails, the function now returns an explicit I/O error code instead of falling through shared cleanup/exit logic, ensuring the caller receives a definite read-failure result at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return explicit -EIO errors for partition lookup and invalid allocation block size failures in hfs_mdb_get(), releasing the buffer before exit when needed.
intent_record.what: The change replaces two goto-based error exits in hfs_mdb_get() with direct error returns: when hfs_part_find(sb, &part_start, &part_size) fails it now returns -EIO instead of jumping to out, and when the allocation block size is invalid it now explicitly calls brelse(bh) and returns -EIO instead of jumping to out_bh.
intent_record.how: At runtime, these paths now propagate an explicit I/O error code instead of falling through shared cleanup labels, and the invalid allocation block size case still releases the buffer head before exiting. This makes the function fail immediately and consistently with -EIO on these error conditions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return -EIO directly on HFS MDB setup/read failures and release the buffer before exiting on an invalid superblock signature.
intent_record.what: The error handling in hfs_mdb_get() was changed from branching to shared cleanup labels with goto to returning -EIO directly in three cases: when sb_set_blocksize() fails, when sb_bread512() returns no buffer, and when mdb->drSigWord does not match HFS_SUPER_MAGIC; additionally, the invalid signature case now explicitly calls brelse(bh) before returning.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now immediately reports I/O failure for these error paths instead of falling through generic labels, and it ensures the buffer head is released when a malformed MDB signature is detected, preventing a leaked buffer reference while preserving failure behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return `-EIO` immediately when HFS bitmap allocation fails instead of falling through the generic cleanup path.
intent_record.what: The error handling after `HFS_SB(sb)->bitmap = kzalloc(8192, GFP_KERNEL);` was changed from `goto out;` to `return -EIO;` when the bitmap allocation fails.
intent_record.how: At runtime, if bitmap allocation fails, the function now exits immediately with an explicit `-EIO` error code instead of jumping to the shared `out` label, ensuring a direct and definite failure result for this allocation error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return -EIO immediately when volume bitmap reading fails so hfs_mdb_get() reports the correct I/O error.
intent_record.what: In hfs_mdb_get(), the error path after a failed sb_bread() call was changed from jumping to the out label with 'goto out' to immediately returning '-EIO'.
intent_record.how: When reading the volume bitmap fails, the function now exits immediately with an explicit I/O error code instead of following the shared cleanup path, ensuring callers receive a direct read-failure result rather than whatever status the out path would produce.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return -EIO immediately when HFS extent or catalog tree opening fails so mount initialization reports the failure correctly.
intent_record.what: In hfs_mdb_get(), the two error branches after failing to open ext_tree or cat_tree were changed from `goto out;` to directly `return -EIO;` while keeping the existing error messages unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, failures to open the extent tree or catalog tree now cause hfs_mdb_get() to immediately return an explicit I/O error code instead of falling through the shared `out` path, ensuring these failures are reported as errors rather than depending on whatever the `out` label would return.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unreachable error-cleanup code from hfs_mdb_get() to simplify the function without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: The patch removes the unreachable error-handling labels and cleanup code at the end of hfs_mdb_get(), specifically deleting the out_bh label with brelse(bh), the out label with hfs_mdb_put(sb), and the final return -EIO after the existing successful return 0.
intent_record.how: At runtime this does not change normal execution from the shown code path because the removed block appears after an unconditional return and is therefore dead code; it eliminates unused error-exit code that could not be reached from the remaining function flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the null-check early return in hfs_mdb_put() so HFS B-tree cleanup always runs for expected valid superblocks.
intent_record.what: The function hfs_mdb_put(struct super_block *sb) was modified by removing the two-line early-return guard that checked `if (!HFS_SB(sb)) return;`, leaving the subsequent `hfs_btree_close(HFS_SB(sb)->ext_tree);` and `hfs_btree_close(HFS_SB(sb)->cat_tree);` calls unconditional.
intent_record.how: At runtime, hfs_mdb_put() will no longer silently do nothing when `HFS_SB(sb)` is null and will always attempt to access and release the HFS superblock's B-tree resources. This makes cleanup unconditional for callers expected to provide a valid HFS superblock and avoids skipping resource release in cases where the guard previously suppressed it.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop hfs_mdb_put() from freeing and nulling the superblock private info so only its subordinate resources are released here and final structure teardown can happen elsewhere.
intent_record.what: The function hfs_mdb_put(struct super_block *sb) was changed by removing two cleanup statements at the end: the kfree(HFS_SB(sb)) call and the assignment sb->s_fs_info = NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this function no longer frees the filesystem-specific superblock info structure or clears the superblock's s_fs_info pointer when hfs_mdb_put() runs; it now only releases nested resources like nls_disk and bitmap, leaving ownership and final teardown of HFS_SB(sb) to some other code path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an HFS-specific kill_sb callback to free superblock private data during unmount and avoid a memory leak.
intent_record.what: A new static function hfs_kill_super(struct super_block *sb) was added, which retrieves struct hfs_sb_info *hsb = HFS_SB(sb), calls kill_block_super(sb), and then frees hsb with kfree(hsb); the hfs_fs_type.kill_sb callback was changed from kill_block_super to hfs_kill_super.
intent_record.how: When the HFS filesystem superblock is torn down, the code now frees the HFS-specific superblock private data after the generic block superblock cleanup runs, preventing that allocated memory from being left behind during unmount or filesystem destruction.

grouping_result.intent: Return -EIO immediately when HFS extent or catalog tree opening fails so mount initialization reports the failure correctly.
Return `-EIO` immediately when HFS bitmap allocation fails instead of falling through the generic cleanup path.
Remove unreachable error-cleanup code from hfs_mdb_get() to simplify the function without changing behavior.
Add an HFS-specific kill_sb callback to free superblock private data during unmount and avoid a memory leak.
Stop hfs_mdb_put() from freeing and nulling the superblock private info so only its subordinate resources are released here and final structure teardown can happen elsewhere.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure HFS mount/metadata initialization propagates explicit -EIO failures immediately for MDB, partition, bitmap, and tree-opening errors so I/O/setup failures are reported correctly.
Fix HFS filesystem unmount and teardown cleanup so superblock-associated resources are always released correctly and memory leaks are avoided.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is a lifetime/cleanup bug where struct hfs_sb_info allocated in sb->s_fs_info leaks on failures before hfs_fill_super() takes ownership. These changes only adjust error codes and immediate failure returns for MDB/partition/bitmap/tree-opening paths; they do not change allocation ownership or cleanup of s_fs_info in the sget_fc()/setup_bdev_super() failure path.

The change only alters error handling for HFS bitmap allocation by returning -EIO earlier. It does not address the mount API ownership/lifetime problem where struct hfs_sb_info in sb->s_fs_info could leak on failures before hfs_fill_super() took ownership.

The change only removes unreachable cleanup code in hfs_mdb_get() for simplification and explicitly does not change behavior. The root cause is a leak of struct hfs_sb_info caused by ownership/cleanup mismatch during new mount API setup before hfs_fill_super() takes over, which this cleanup removal does not address.

The changes directly address HFS superblock private-state cleanup and memory leak prevention by ensuring `s_fs_info` is freed via an HFS-specific `kill_sb` path and teardown runs reliably. That matches the root cause, which is leaked `struct hfs_sb_info` due to ownership/cleanup being tied only to `hfs_mdb_put()` during new mount API failure paths.

The root cause is that filesystem-private state in sb->s_fs_info was being freed only via hfs_mdb_put(), causing ownership/cleanup mismatches and leaks on mount failure paths. This change directly alters hfs_mdb_put() so it no longer frees/nulls the top-level superblock private info, separating subordinate cleanup from final structure teardown, which is exactly part of fixing that ownership problem.

candidates.rationale: Using the generic block-superblock teardown omitted HFS-specific cleanup of sb->s_fs_info in failure/unmount paths, which directly caused the leaked struct hfs_sb_info after the new mount API started allocating it earlier.

This early null check made hfs_mdb_put() depend on HFS_SB(sb) being present and reinforced the assumption that cleanup of filesystem-private state only happened through this path, contributing to missed teardown when ownership/cleanup ordering changed.

This line shows the old design where freeing the superblock-private struct was tied exclusively to hfs_mdb_put(); that ownership model became invalid once s_fs_info was allocated before hfs_fill_super() ownership, leading to leaks on earlier failure paths.

This statement demonstrates that final teardown of sb->s_fs_info was performed only inside hfs_mdb_put(), which was not guaranteed to run for sget_fc()/setup_bdev_super() failures, thus embodying the leak-prone cleanup model.

vuln_statements.explanation: Using the generic kill_block_super teardown meant HFS-specific private state in sb->s_fs_info was not freed on teardown paths introduced by the new mount API, directly enabling the leak of struct hfs_sb_info when allocation occurred before hfs_fill_super() ownership.

This line tied freeing of the filesystem-private struct exclusively to hfs_mdb_put(), but after the new mount API allocated sb->s_fs_info earlier, failure paths in sget_fc()/setup_bdev_super() could bypass hfs_mdb_put(), causing the allocated struct hfs_sb_info to leak.

This statement confirms that final cleanup ownership of sb->s_fs_info existed only inside hfs_mdb_put(); because earlier mount failure paths did not necessarily reach that function, the design left allocated HFS private state uncollected.

bic_trace_step.reason: The provided function is the old mount path using `get_sb_bdev(..., hfs_fill_super)`, not the newer mount API described in the root cause. In `hfs_fill_super()`, the filesystem-private state is allocated and assigned locally: `sbi = kmalloc(sizeof(struct hfs_sb_info), GFP_KERNEL);` followed by `sb->s_fs_info = sbi;`. On failure paths inside this function, it is explicitly freed with `kfree(sbi);` at `bail3`, and the path after `hfs_mdb_get(sb)` failure goes through `bail2`/`bail3`, while the later root-inode failure path does `hfs_mdb_put(sb);` and then `kfree(sbi);`. So the specific vulnerable construct from the root cause—allocation in `sb->s_fs_info` before `hfs_fill_super()` ownership combined with cleanup only in `hfs_mdb_put()` during `sget_fc()`/`setup_bdev_super()` failures—is not present here, because this code predates the new mount API and does not use `sget_fc()`/`setup_bdev_super()`. At the same time, it also does not contain the later fix for that new-API leak scenario; it is simply an older implementation where that exact bug does not arise.

    [PATCH] hfs, hfsplus: don't leak s_fs_info and fix an oops
    
    This patch fixes the leak of sb->s_fs_info in both the HFS and HFS+
    modules.  In addition to this, it fixes an oops happening when trying to
    mount a non-hfsplus filesystem using hfsplus.  This patch is from Roman
    Zippel, based off patches sent by myself.
    
    Signed-off-by: Colin Leroy
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant cleanup logic in `hfs_mdb_put()` clearly enough to decide. The vulnerability root cause is that `sb->s_fs_info` (the `struct hfs_sb_info`) was allocated earlier but not freed on cleanup paths, causing a leak. In this commit, `hfs_mdb_put()` now explicitly handles that state: it first guards against a NULL private pointer with `if (!HFS_SB(sb)) return;`, and after releasing the B-trees and buffers it adds `kfree(HFS_SB(sb));` followed by `sb->s_fs_info = NULL;`. Those added lines are exactly the missing cleanup for the leaked filesystem-private state, and the NULL guard also prevents dereferencing an absent `s_fs_info`. Therefore the vulnerable construct (missing free of `sb->s_fs_info`) is no longer present, and the fix is present in this function.
